messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert - auth-service 5xx/401 spike detected. 3 distinct IP ranges, sudden surge in token validation failures. Paging oncall (maria). See alert: https://pager/redwood/incidents/1813001234

maria (oncall): seeing it, joining. pulling logs now. any customer-facing impact?

lee (sre): tails show lots of `invalid_token` from 34.83.12.0/24 and 178.62.45.0/24. Spike started ~12:03 UTC. Not all requests correlate to known client ids.

sam (sec): possible token replay or leaked debug logs. Did anything touch debug logging last deploy?

tony (auth-eng): we shipped a minor rollback yesterday with extra debug flags in `auth-debug` feature branch. I need a sec to check CI artifacts.

maria (oncall): mark as potential PII/secret exposure until we know. Sam, can you join to triage?

sam (sec): on it. Lee, can you preserve logs and snapshot the auth instance? don't restart anything yet.

lee (sre): snapshot created (ami-0abc1234), logs zipped to s3://redwood-incidents/1813001234/logs.tar.gz. Access restricted to sec+oncall.

tony (auth-eng): found CI job `deploy-auth-debug` that uploaded `auth-debug.log` to s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/builds/8787/debug.log. Log contains `Authorization: Bearer` headers and what looks like session tokens. not all tokens look active but some match recent validation attempts.

sam (sec): confirmed token strings in the artifact correspond to token hashes in the spike. This is confirmed exposure. Escalating to SEV2-security. We need immediate mitigation: rotate affected keys/tokens, revoke sessions, and block offending IP ranges.

maria (oncall): > Action plan: 1) block IP ranges 34.83.12.0/24 & 178.62.45.0/24 at edge, 2) revoke tokens and rotate service credentials for auth, 3) take CI artifact offline and audit who accessed it, 4) customer impact assessment and communication. Assign owners: lee->edge block & snapshot, tony->rotate keys, sam->audit & legal notify, jess->draft customer comms.

lee (sre): applied temporary denylist at edge: `iptables` rules on edge-proxy and updated WAF rule ID 89321 to block ranges. Confirmed drop rates for those ranges now ~100%.

deploy-bot: deploy status: rule update -> success (edge-proxy-cluster v4).

tony (auth-eng): running rotation script for auth tokens: ```./scripts/rotate_service_tokens.sh --service auth --scope sessions --reason "leaked-debug-logs-181300"``` will take ~2 mins to revoke active sessions and issue rotated keys. I will avoid global restart; tokens revoked via token-service.

tony (auth-eng): rotation complete. Issued new service key (redacted). Token-service reports 4.2k sessions revoked. Monitoring for errors.

sam (sec): auditing access logs for S3 artifact. Found two external IPs downloaded debug.log ~11:50 UTC: 34.83.12.45 and 178.62.45.89 via ephemeral CI creds. Opening tickets with CI provider to trace how artifact ACL was set to public.

jess (support): drafting customer notice. Preliminary severity: potential exposure of session tokens for subset of customers. Need to confirm which customer tokens were in the file. Sam, can you provide customer list quick?

sam (sec): pulling token->customer map, will post PII-safe summary in ~15. Avoid naming customers in channel.

maria (oncall): do we need to rotate any long-lived keys or just session tokens?

tony (auth-eng): initial pass focused on session tokens. We'll rotate service keys that might have been embedded in CI per our inventory: rotated `ci-deployer` key pair and rotated the `auth-debug` feature key. Running validation to ensure no regression.

sam (sec): also recommend forcing password resets or re-issuing refresh grants for affected customers if customer tokens present. Will coordinate with support.

jess (support): OK prepping templated notice: short, what happened, actions taken, recommended customer actions (rotate API keys, re-auth). Will route to legal for signoff.

lee (sre): monitoring auth errors: 401s have dropped back to baseline after rotation and edge blocks. No new suspicious spikes in last 20m.

maria (oncall): creating incident record and SEV2-security timeline. Sam, please add root cause hypothesis and next steps. We'll move to postmortem channel once stable.

sam (sec): root cause preliminary: CI pipeline accidentally uploaded debug artifact with Authorization headers due to missing sanitizer step in feature branch. Remediation: fail CI on any log artifact that contains `Authorization` header. I'll open a PR to the CI lint rules.

tony (auth-eng): PR to sanitize logs: https://git/redwood/infra/ci/pulls/432 - adds redaction, fails on footer tokens.

maria (oncall): good. Final status for channel: mitigation complete, edge blocks in place, tokens rotated, artifact removed, security audit in progress, customer comms draft circulating. Moving to monitoring state. We'll reconvene for handoff to follow-up owner list in 1 hour. :lock:

incident-bot: Incident 1813001234 -> SEV2-Security mitigated -> status: monitoring.

maria (oncall): handing off to sam (sec) for follow-up and to jess for customer comms. If anything new triggers, reopen here or escalate. Thanks team. :eyes:
